condition: Perianal Crohn’s disease — complex fistula with abscess
summary: 31-year-old woman with Crohn’s colitis, perianal pain and purulent discharge from two external openings with a fluctuant posterior swelling. EUA, drainage and loose seton; MRI pelvis; then anti-TNF. No fistulotomy of a complex Crohn’s fistula and no sphincterotomy.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Painful swelling and discharge near the back passage
inputs.hpi: Crohn’s colitis on mesalazine only (declined biologics last year). Three weeks of perianal discharge from two openings, and for 4 days a painful swelling behind the anus with fevers. Bowels 3 times a day, some mucus.

exam.other: Perianal: two external openings at 5 and 7 o’clock discharging pus; fluctuant, tender swelling in the posterior midline extending to both sides. Skin tags. DRE not tolerated.

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — anorectal abscess, fistula-in-ano and rectovaginal fistula
guideline.section: Abscess: prompt drainage. Crohn’s fistula: loose seton for complex disease; MRI or EUS to define anatomy; fistulotomy only for simple, low fistulas
guideline.citation: Gaertner WB, Burgess PL, Davids JS, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for the management of anorectal abscess, fistula-in-ano, and rectovaginal fistula. Dis Colon Rectum. 2022;65:964–985.

guideline.name: BSG consensus guidelines — management of inflammatory bowel disease in adults
guideline.section: Perianal Crohn’s: MRI pelvis; EUA, drainage and seton; anti-TNF after sepsis control
guideline.citation: Lamb CA, Kennedy NA, Raine T, et al. British Society of Gastroenterology consensus guidelines on the management of inflammatory bowel disease in adults. Gut. 2019;68(Suppl 3):s1–s106.

rationale: Permutation: perianal phenotype. Uses the generic "Other / general surgical" template because the web has no presentation-level template for perianal pain or swelling (only diagnosis-named ones). Checks that the complex-fistula plan is seton-based and never a lay-open or sphincterotomy.
